context:
Goal: no reviewed PR waits, and a tool, not a hand, keeps it so.
Problem (goal): PRs are made about 7 times faster than they merge. Lanes find gaps, each gap becomes a new lane, and the batch runner builds each batch by hand. You called the hold options bandaids (21:44 CST).
Based on (notes): the coordinator counts about 380 PRs opened (#1384 to #1763) against 26 batches of 1-5 lanes.
Based on (notes): root cause found by runner 8: a coordinator handoff line with no ruling, "a guard or check change batches alone", put most done PRs one per batch, at 21-37 min of CI each. The coordinator withdrew it at 21:46 CST. Runner 8 now batches every clean done PR together and builds the next batch while one runs.
Departs from: main, where each finding becomes its own step and lane, and the runner builds each batch by hand from messages — the merge tool batches every reviewed PR itself, and a lane's findings ride in its own PR or one follow-up per topic.
Meanwhile: your hold on new lanes stays, except lanes that land these fixes.

options.gain: The queue drains, and merges keep pace with reviews.
options.how: The merge tool builds each batch from PR state: every PR with a done review record on its live head and a lane lint pass. It splits a red batch itself, and builds the next batch while one runs, on top of #1561's ledger.
options.label: The merge tool builds each batch (recommended)

options.how: A lane's findings join its next commit, or one follow-up PR per topic, not one new lane each.
options.label: Findings ride in their lane (recommended)
options.lose: Findings land bundled, so one red finding holds the others.

options.how: Every runner and coordinator report gives three counts: reviewed PRs waiting past one batch cycle, open PRs with no next act, and finished lanes not archived. A count not read says unknown.
options.label: Backlog counts in every report (recommended)
options.lose: A few more lines in each report.

ref: steps pr-backlog-clear and pr-state-is-on-the-pr; #1561 (the PR ledger)
title: Make merges keep pace with reviews: which parts do you want?
why: The coordinator recommends all three: part a alone drains the queue but does not slow new PRs, and part b alone does not drain it.
